findings.title: render :show runs before canonical_url is set
findings.body: perform_show_response now calls render :show inside the HTML branch (topics_controller.rb:500). TopicsController#show only calls canonical_url after perform_show_response returns (line 87). Previously the HTML branch did not render, so Rails implicit render ran after the action finished and the layout still saw @canonical_url. render evaluates the show template and layout immediately, so @canonical_url is still nil and every topic HTML response loses its canonical link. This is a silent site-wide regression, not limited to unsubscribe. Move the render back out of the shared method, or set the canonical URL before rendering.

findings.title: Unsubscribe mutates notification state on a cookie-authenticated GET
findings.body: config/routes.rb registers topics#unsubscribe as GET (t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe), and the action writes TopicUser.notification_level at topics_controller.rb:107-113 with no per-user token. Topic#unsubscribe_url (topic.rb:719) is only /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe, the same for every recipient, unlike the existing digest link email/unsubscribe/:key. Rails forgery protection does not cover GET, so any page can include that URL as an image or link and, for a logged-in victim, downgrade or mute the topic. Email prefetchers and link scanners that send the user's cookies will do the same without a click. Logged-out recipients are only redirected to login, so the link does not identify or unsubscribe the person who was emailed. The Ember route never calls an unsubscribe API; it only loads the topic. A safe design is a signed, user-specific token, or a GET confirmation page plus a POST that uses TopicUser.change.

findings.title: Unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watchers and is not idempotent
findings.body: If notification_level is above regular (tracking=2 or watching=3), unsubscribe sets regular (1); otherwise it sets muted (0). Watching is what causes an email on every new post, and the new copy promises a full stop: server.en.yml unsubscribe_link says "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and client.en.yml topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications says "You will stop receiving notifications". After one request those users are still at regular, so replies, mentions, and quotes still notify. The transition is also not idempotent: a second GET (refresh, duplicate fetch, or a scanner request plus the user's click) sees regular and mutes. Outcome depends on how many times the URL is hit, and mute hides the topic from the user's lists, which is stronger than stopping email and is never explained. Always set muted (or another single terminal level) through TopicUser.change, and make repeat requests a no-op.

findings.title: Missing TopicUser 500s, and save! does not record an explicit choice
findings.body: unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If the logged-in viewer has no topic_users row (the URL is not bound to the email recipient; any logged-in user who can see the topic can open it), tu is nil and this raises NoMethodError. tu.save! also bypasses TopicUser.change, which is what sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, sets notifications_changed_at, creates a missing row, and publishes /topic/:id on MessageBus. The mailer creates the recipient row with TopicUser.change(last_emailed_post_number:) and does not set a reason, so reason often stays nil. update_last_read then auto-upgrades notification_level back to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and view time exceeds the auto-track threshold, and TopicUser.auto_track does the same when reason is nil. The unsubscribe can be silently undone on a later visit, and other open tabs are not notified. Use TopicUser.change so a missing row is created and the user's choice is sticky.

findings.title: Unsubscribe template name does not match the route
findings.body: The route is registered as topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (app-route-map.js.es6:13). The new controller, route, and view are all topic-unsubscribe, which Ember resolves as topicUnsubscribe / template topic-unsubscribe. This template lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which compiles to the name topic/unsubscribe (nested route topic.unsubscribe). No code renders that name, and there is no templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs. The view also does not set templateName. After the Rails shell loads, the confirmation screen is blank: the stop-notifications copy and topic-notifications-button never appear, so the user cannot see or correct the level the GET just wrote. Move the template to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route under topic and move the controller and view to match.

findings.title: No spec covers unsubscribe behavior or the new email link
findings.body: The only test change passes unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" so I18n can interpolate unsubscribe_link. The example at line 179 still only checks that the user-preferences URL is in the body; it never asserts the per-topic URL or the new "click here" sentence. There is no request/controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching versus regular, a second GET, slug redirect, logged-out access, or CSRF. The broken level transitions and the nil TopicUser crash can ship without a failing test.
